paper_metadata.title: Quantum Architecture Search for Quantum Monte Carlo Integration via Conditional Parameterized Circuits with Application to Finance

summary: The paper proposes conditional parameterized quantum circuits (CPQCs) for implementing payoff functions in amplitude-estimation-based option pricing. Using a genetic architecture search (20 generations, population 48, ~5.5 hours classical training), the authors produce PQCs whose CPQC form reduces function-evaluation circuit complexity from O(n log n) to O(n) for basket options; for example, a CPQC instance at n=14 requires 92 CNOT gates and depth 151. Results are demonstrated via noiseless simulation and circuit resource comparisons rather than full amplitude estimation experiments.

experiments.description: Genetically trained parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) for European vanilla call option payoff approximation, and its conditional parameterized quantum circuit (CPQC) version used for quantum Monte Carlo integration / amplitude estimation subroutine comparison against bitwise quantum arithmetic.

algorithm.variant: PQC/CPQC function-approximation subroutine for amplitude estimation; genetic structure learning with variable ansatzes
algorithm.ansatz: custom hardware-native parameterized circuit with rotational encoding blocks and parameterized blocks
algorithm.optimizer: PennyLane RMSProp optimizer; classical genetic selection/mutation loop
algorithm.convergence_criteria: new structure accepted if cost decreased; if cost increased, accepted with probability exp(-5(c_new-c_old)/c_old); gate removed if cost increase below 1%

problem_formulation.encoding_details: asset price discretized on n control qubits; payoff function encoded via rotational gates and controlled rotations in CPQC
problem_formulation.objective_function: approximate European call payoff f_+(X)=max(X-K,0) as a quantum model for use in amplitude estimation

problem_instance.description: European vanilla call option payoff approximation

dataset_specification.description: discretized asset prices shown in figure/caption; strike K=100

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: asset price discretization; scaled discretization x_k in [0,2π) mentioned generally
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: function approximation shown against truth; comparison of CNOT count and depth versus IBM quantum arithmetic approach across control-qubit sizes

hardware.transpilation_target: CNOT and U(θ,φ,λ) decomposition for resource counting

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: discounting of expected payoff on classical device
implementation_details.total_execution_time: about 5.5 hours for the full genetic search on a dual Intel Xeon Gold 6240R system with 48 cores

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming amplitude estimation subroutine and efficient state/function preparation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speed-up in convergence rate of AE over classical Monte Carlo; the CPQC is a function-implementation subroutine enabling this setting.

speedup_claims.factor: lower cnot count and depth than bitwise quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.conditions: for the compared control-qubit sizes shown in Fig. 5
speedup_claims.caveats: Exact baseline counts are only shown graphically; the paper reports the CPQC comparison qualitatively and via scaling plots.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: bitwise quantum arithmetic for option pricing
speedup_claims.conditions: for the CPQC construction with rotational encodings
speedup_claims.caveats: This is the paper's stated scaling for the CPQC; the baseline arithmetic method is also O(n) in the vanilla case.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n) for CPQC function implementation; compared against O(n) bitwise arithmetic for vanilla option in the cited baseline
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(N)) Monte Carlo convergence for classical estimation; baseline quantum arithmetic for option pricing O(n) in qubit register size n

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not estimated; paper only compares circuit depth and CNOT scaling of CPQC vs quantum arithmetic implementation
limiting_factors: No full AE algorithm execution or runtime benchmarking
State preparation and distribution loading assumed given
Pretraining cost (5.5 hours classical search) not included in advantage analysis

notes: Hardware is not tied to a named QPU; experiments are presented as circuit constructions and resource comparisons, so simulator/noisy hardware is not explicitly specified.
num_qubits and circuit depth are not given as a single fixed value for this experiment; they vary with the control-qubit count n and are shown only in scaling plots.
Speedup order is inferred from the paper's stated quadratic convergence improvement of amplitude estimation over classical Monte Carlo.
Authors discuss theoretical quadratic speedup of amplitude estimation but do not experimentally demonstrate runtime advantage
Experiments only show circuit resource reductions for payoff implementation
